items.summary_1line: This technical report presents MNN-Pocket-0.3B, a compact 300M-parameter dense language model designed for efficient on-device deployment and supporting context lengths of up to 32K tokens. With an INT4 deployment foo...
items.editor_note: 스레드는 가장 작은 모델인 INT4 경로를 갖춘 300M 온디바이스 모델로 시작한다.

items.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report

items.editor_note: 자기회귀 방식이 일반적인 것과 다른 디코딩 접근인 희소 디퓨전 LM이 추가된다.

items.title: Beam Model Technical Report
items.summary_1line: A technical report introducing Beam, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters for coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks, with a 1M-token context window and a large-scale asynchronous RL post-training run.
items.editor_note: 가장 큰 모델로, 에이전트 작업을 겨냥한 501B 희소 MoE가 추가된다. 1M 토큰 컨텍스트와 비동기 RL 사후 학습을 갖췄다.

items.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
items.summary_1line: Introduces SAG-Mem, a conversational memory framework that stores full dialogue messages in chunks with a lexical index and no LLM processing, reporting top scores of 83.08 on LoCoMo and 80.20 on LongMemEval.
items.editor_note: 최신 항목은 모델에서 에이전트 메모리로 초점을 옮겨, 원본 대화에 대한 어휘 기반 검색과 벤치마크 점수를 다룬다.

editorial.tldr: This is a loose thread of unrelated arXiv technical reports, not one developing event. It opened Nov 9 with MNN-Pocket-0.3B, a 300M on-device model, then added sparse MoE models: the Clover diffusion LM (35B total, 3B active) and Beam (501.3B total, 23.4B active, 1M-token context).
editorial.whats_new: SAG-Mem-1.0's report (Nov 24) describes a conversational memory framework that stores raw dialogue chunks behind a lexical index with no LLM processing, reporting 83.08 on LoCoMo and 80.20 on LongMemEval.
editorial.why_it_matters: The reports span different serving shapes: sub-1B INT4 on-device models, sparse MoE models up to 501B, and a memory layer that skips LLM calls at write time, each with its own runtime and cost profile.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat these as research reads. If you run agent memory, benchmark SAG-Mem's no-LLM chunk-and-index approach against your summarization pipeline on LoCoMo or LongMemEval before paying for write-time LLM calls.

beats.headline: MNN-Pocket-0.3B targets on-device deployment at 300M parameters
beats.summary: A compact dense model with 32K context and an INT4 deployment path.

beats.headline: Clover and Beam report sparse mixture-of-experts models at two scales
beats.summary: Clover is a 35B/3B-active diffusion LM with thinking mode; Beam is a 501.3B/23.4B-active model for coding and agentic tasks with a 1M-token context.

beats.headline: SAG-Mem-1.0: agent memory from raw chunks and a lexical index
beats.summary: No LLM summarization at write time; reported 83.08 on LoCoMo and 80.20 on LongMemEval.

open_questions: Are the MNN-Pocket-0.3B, Clover, or Beam weights released under a license that permits commercial use?
Do mainstream inference servers support Clover's diffusion decoding, or does it need a custom runtime?
Do independent evals reproduce MNN-Pocket-0.3B's reported quality at INT4?
Does Beam's 1M-token context hold up on long-context agentic benchmarks run outside the authors' lab?
Do SAG-Mem's LoCoMo and LongMemEval scores hold up against LLM-summarized memory baselines under independent replication?
